[[Smouha Sporting Club|Smouha]] | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2010–11 Egyptian Premier League|2010–11]] | nextseason = [[2012–13 Egyptian Premier League|2012–13]] }} The '''2011–12 Egyptian Premier League''' was the fifty-fifth season of the [[Egyptian Premier League]] since its establishment in 1948. The season began on 14 October 2011, with a total of 19 teams contesting the league. [[Al-Ahly S.C.|Al Ahly]] won the last seven league titles. This season, the league increased from 16 to 19 teams due to no relegation in the [[2010–11 Egyptian Premier League|2010–11]] season as a result of the [[2011 Egyptian revolution]]. Three teams were promoted from the [[Egyptian Second Division|second division]]. Following the [[Port Said Stadium disaster]] on 1 February 2012, the season was suspended.{{cite news|author=Abdel-Rahman Hussein|title=Egypt football match violence: dozens dead and hundreds injured|work=The Guardian|location=UK|date=2 February 2012|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/feb/01/egypt-football-match-violence-dead}} At that time, teams had played between 14 and 17 games out of 30. [[Haras El-Hodood Club|Haras El-Hodood]] was in first place with a 12–1–1 record. This result was considered a significant surprise by ''[[Al Ahram]]''.{{cite news|title=Harras El-Hodoud want Champions League clarification|author=Mahmoud Elassal|date=11 March 2012|work=Ahram Online|url=http://english.ahram.org.eg/NewsContent/6/51/36462/Sports/Egyptian-Football/Harras-ElHodoud-want-Champions-League-clarificatio.aspx|access-date=11 March 2012}} On 10 March 2012, a decision was reached to cancel the remainder of the season. == Teams == [[Union Alexandria|Al Ittihad Al Sakandary]], [[Smouha Sporting Club|Smouha]] and [[Arab Contractors SC|Al Mokawloon Al Arab]] were the worst three teams in [[2010–11 Egyptian Premier League|2010–11]] but were not relegated to the 2011–12 [[Egyptian Second Division]]. Three teams were promoted from the [[2010–11 Egyptian Second Division]] – [[El Dakhleya]], [[Ghazl El-Mehalla|Ghazl El Mahalla]], and [[Telephonat Bani Sweif]] – bringing the league up to 19 teams Alexandria|Al Ittihad Al Sakandary]] *Fewest clean sheets: '''0''' **[[ENPPI Club|Enppi]] **[[Tala'ea El-Gaish SC|Tala'ea El Gaish]] ==Cancellation== On 10 March 2012, a decision was reached to cancel the remainder of the season.{{cite news|title=Egypt's Premier League cancelled|publisher=BBC|date=10 March 2012|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17324997|access-date=11 March 2012}} A spokesperson for the [[Egyptian Football Association]] said the decision was made because there was insufficient time to play the remaining games before the [[Egypt national football team|national team]] was scheduled to compete in the [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics|2012 Olympics]] and qualifiers for the [[2013 Africa Cup of Nations]]. [[Farouk Ga’afar]], coach of [[Tala'ea El-Gaish SC|El-Gaish]] strongly criticized the decision saying the decision would cost the country a lot of money and that "people sitting in coffee shops could make a better decision."{{cite news|title=El-Geish coach condemns EFA for league cancellation|date=11 March 2012|work=Ahram Online|url=http://english.ahram.org.eg/NewsContent/6/51/36491/Sports/Egyptian-Football/ElGeish-coach-condemns-EFA-for-league-cancellation.aspx|access-date=11 March 2012}} It was the fifth time that Egypt has cancelled a season of football; previously 1954–55, 1970–71, 1973–74, and 1989–90 were cancelled for a variety of reasons. At the same time, it was announced that 18 teams would compete in a friendly tournament "Martyrs Cup" to raise money for families of those killed in Port Said incident. [[Al-Masry Club|Al Masry]], the home team whose fans rioted in Port Said, leaving 72 people dead and 150 injured, was barred from the tournament. Al Ahly, the visiting team during the attack, has been invited but has not confirmed whether they will participate or not. The tournament is scheduled to commence on 29 March with [[Round-robin tournament|round robin]] play. The league will be divided into two groups, and the games will take place in empty stadiums owned by the Egyptian Army.{{cite news|title=Egyptian Premier League season cancelled|date=11 March 2012|work=Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/news/2012/March/11/egyptian-premier-league-season-cancelled/|access-date=11 March 2012}} The top two teams from each group will advance to the semi-finals for a single elimination event. The final is scheduled for 18 May. The [[Egypt Cup]] is expected to take place as normal, with Al Masry barred from competition.{{cite news|title=Egyptian PL cancelled after deadly violence |work=SuperSport|date=11 March 2012|url=http://www.supersport.com/football/africa/news/120311/Egyptian_PL_cancelled_after_deadly_violence|access-date=11 March 2012}} Under normal circumstances, the league's top two teams get to participate in the [[African Champions League]]. It was not immediately clear if league leaders El-Hodood and Al-Ahly would be declared as the league's top two teams and invited to participate in the Champions League. "I am not against the league cancellation but I want to know: Will we be considered as the league champions?" asked El-Hodoud coach [[Tarek El-Ashry]]. In the end, Al-Ahly and [[Zamalek SC|Zamalek]], who were the 2010-11 League Champions and runners-up, were selected to represent Egypt.
